answer: A practical defense is to make each agent earn a costly, verifiable reputation before it can trade. Like a sonnet, the rules are tight: an agent must complete useful work and hold a stake that is lost if it misbehaves. A lantern of public attestations then lights up real history, so a newcomer cannot fake trust overnight. When a tide of fresh identities arrives, the market demands that same earned stake from each one, turning cheap mass creation into an expensive, slow climb that honest agents already made.
